question: Where is the thymus located in the human body?

options.A: In the upper chest behind the sternum
options.B: In the lower right side of the abdomen
options.C: Attached directly to the posterior liver
options.D: Wrapped around the trachea in the neck

explanation: The thymus sits safely within the superior mediastinum, directly behind the breastbone and in front of the heart. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h1)

question: What are the two main structural zones found inside each thymic lobule?
explanation: Each lobule of the thymus is clearly divided into an outer cortex and an inner medulla. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which type of immune cell completes its maturation inside the thymus?
explanation: The primary job of the thymus is to take immature cells from bone marrow and mature them into functional T-lymphocytes. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h2)

question: Why does the thymus destroy many developing T-cells before they enter the bloodstream?

options.A: To clear space when the person eats too much dietary protein
options.B: To turn them into red blood cells when the bone marrow gets tired
options.C: To produce extra energy for the heart muscle during heavy exercise
options.D: To eliminate cells that fail recognition tests or attack healthy body tissues

explanation: The thymus removes T-cells that cannot recognize body markers or that might mistakenly attack healthy body tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which hormone is produced by the thymus gland?
explanation: Thymosin is one of the key hormones secreted by the thymus to help drive T-cell development and immune function. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of hormones like thymosin and thymopoietin?

options.A: To support the maturation and development of T-cells
options.B: To control how fast the kidneys filter liquid waste
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell creation in the bone marrow
options.D: To regulate daily sleep and wake cycles in adults

explanation: Thymic hormones act on developing lymphocytes to ensure they mature correctly and support immune competence. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h3)

question: What happens to the size of the thymus gland as a person grows from childhood into late adulthood?

options.A: It stays the exact same size throughout life
options.B: It disappears completely by age five
options.C: It grows much larger to match adult body mass
options.D: It gradually shrinks and is replaced by fatty tissue

explanation: After puberty, the thymus undergoes involution, shrinking in size as active tissue gives way to fat and connective tissue. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h4)

question: How does the shrinking of the thymus in older adults primarily affect their immune system?

options.A: It lowers the production of brand new naive T-cells
options.B: It causes an immediate loss of all immunity to childhood diseases
options.C: It stops the liver from making blood-clotting proteins
options.D: It forces the bone marrow to produce too many white blood cells

explanation: As the thymus shrinks with age, fewer new T-cells are produced, and the body relies more on existing immune memory cells. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h4)

question: Which autoimmune condition is frequently associated with tumors of the thymus gland?
explanation: A high percentage of patients with thymomas or thymic abnormalities also suffer from myasthenia gravis, a disorder causing muscle weakness. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary health consequence for an infant born with DiGeorge syndrome who lacks a functioning thymus?

options.A: Severe immunodeficiency due to a lack of mature T-cells
options.B: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells leading to thick blood
options.C: Permanent failure of the kidneys to filter urine
options.D: Complete inability to produce breast milk digestion enzymes

explanation: Without a thymus, the body cannot properly mature T-cells, leaving the infant highly vulnerable to infections. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T3#BMP111_U6_T3_h5)
